name: Kang-Petrov Arms KPA-15 'Diaspora'
description:
The KPA-15 Diaspora is the most widely manufactured assault rifle on GLMZ. Kang-Petrov Arms designed it for mass production — stamped steel components, minimal machining, and a modular architecture that allows regional factories to produce the weapon with varying levels of sophistication. The base model is a straightforward 5.56mm gas-operated rifle with polymer furniture and a 30-round magazine. Optional BCI-link modules snap into a rail-mounted interface port.

Production variants range from bare-bones militia grade (Φ800) to corporate-contract models with integrated optics and recoil compensation (Φ3,200). This range makes the Diaspora the most democratic weapon in production — it arms everyone from Tier 1 neighborhood watches to Tier 3 corporate auxiliary forces. Kang-Petrov licenses production to fourteen regional manufacturers, ensuring supply even when trade routes collapse.

The weapon's reliability is adequate rather than exceptional, but replacement parts are available everywhere. When a Diaspora breaks, you fix it with parts from any other Diaspora. This interchangeability is its greatest asset and the reason it has proliferated across every conflict zone on the planet.
legality: Widely available — minimal restrictions in most zones
specifications:
caliber: 5.56mm standard
effective_range: 400m
rate_of_fire: 700 rpm (cyclic)
magazine_capacity: 30 rounds
weight: 3.2 kg
tactical_use: The KPA-15 is a volume weapon — its tactical advantage is availability, not superiority. In protracted conflicts where supply chains matter more than individual engagements, the Diaspora's ubiquitous parts and ammunition keep forces armed when premium weapons sit idle waiting for proprietary components. Smart operators pair baseline Diasporas with aftermarket optics and BCI modules to achieve 80% of a premium rifle's capability at 25% of the cost.
cultural_context: The Diaspora is the rifle of the masses. Its name reflects the weapon's presence in every displaced community, every refugee defense force, every neighborhood militia across GLMZ. Kang-Petrov's decision to license production broadly has made them less profitable per unit but enormously influential — when people think 'rifle,' they think KPA-15. Street murals frequently feature the Diaspora's distinctive angular profile as a symbol of armed community self-defense.
story_hooks: One of the fourteen licensed KPA-15 manufacturers has been producing weapons with deliberately weakened firing pins — the rifles function for approximately 200 rounds before catastrophic failure.
A community militia discovers that the BCI-link modules on their Diasporas are transmitting location data to a corponation that plans to annex their territory.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian, deliberately simple assault rifle with a distinctly modular aesthetic. The KPA-15 presents a clean, angular silhouette dominated by stamped steel components and polymer furniture. Its design philosophy is visible in every line—no unnecessary curves, minimal ornamentation, everything optimized for factory production and field repair. The rifle has a squared-off receiver, a flat-top picatinny rail system, and a characteristic modular rail interface port on the left side of the lower receiver that marks it immediately as a Diaspora variant.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 94.5 cm (carbine config), Barrel length: 41.6 cm, Width across furniture: 8.2 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Noticeably light in hand—3.2 kg feels almost hollow compared to heavier military platforms. The balance is slightly forward-heavy due to barrel and gas tube, but deliberately manageable for prolonged use. Has the feel of a weapon designed for sustained volume fire rather than precision work.
physical_description.primary_material: Stamped and welded steel receiver and barrel group, polymer lower furniture, aluminum rail segments, synthetic polymer handguard and stock
physical_description.finish: Matte black phosphate coating on steel components—utilitarian and non-reflective. The polymer furniture shows a slightly textured, dull dark gray finish typical of injection-molded components. Some variants display visible stamping marks and assembly seams from mass production.
physical_description.color_scheme: Predominantly matte black steel with dark gray polymer accents. Minimal branding—silver or dark gray markings only
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized pistol grip with subtle vertical ribbing for retention. Polymer handguard has a lightly textured surface designed for gloved operation. The magazine well is oversized for easy manipulation even in tactical gear.
distinctive_features: Characteristic modular BCI-link interface port on left side of receiver—recessed rectangular mounting point with four threaded holes
Flat-top picatinny rail running the full length of upper receiver
Stamped steel construction visible as subtle linear patterns and slight surface imperfections
Universal mag well designed for rapid magazine changes
Gas tube and charging handle positioned for ambidextrous operation
Simplified front and rear iron sights—polymer, low-profile, field-replaceable
Magazine catch and release buttons slightly oversized for tactical glove compatibility
Ventilation cuts in polymer furniture to reduce weight without sacrificing durability
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: KANG-PETROV ARMS logo stamped in small silver text on left side of receiver above the magazine well. Serial number plate (stainless steel) mounted on left side of lower receiver with Φ-currency denomination and production date codes. Regional manufacturer variant stamps appear on the barrel beneath the gas tube.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained examples show light wear on high-contact points—charging handle, magazine well edges, and grip area. Battle-worn variants display scratched polymer furniture, scuffed rail finishes, and visible component replacement (mixing parts from different production runs). Even heavily used Diasporas maintain function due to stamped simplicity—rarely pristine, always serviceable.
